cause: The transcription keeps a quality but drops the sub-part or place it belongs to (base, apex, margin, throat, inside or beneath, upper part, veins, cells, wing, prickles, angles), so the annotator gives the quality to the whole organ.
remedy: Prompt: 'When the words name a part of the organ (base, apex, tip, margin, throat, inside/within, beneath/above, upper part, angles, veins, costules, cells of X, wing, prickles), make that part the row's part and the organ its whole. Never give the quality to the whole organ.' Annotator: if the source span holds a place word from flora_context_words.tsv (at the base, at apex, at throat, inside, beneath, dans la partie supérieure, along <veins>, except) and the row's part is the bare organ, fill the place slot or hold the row. Map 'inside/within' to adaxial. In '<surface> glabrescent except <hair word> along <veins>', the hair word goes on the veins.
detectable: yes: the source span contains a place or sub-part word ('at the base', 'at apex', 'margins', 'throat', 'inside', 'beneath', 'cells of', 'wing', 'along', 'except') that does not appear in the grounded bearer or the place slot
example: '± rounded or cuneate at the base' became leaf lamina cuneate; it should be leaf lamina base (PO:0008019) cuneate, value_qualifier approximately

cause: A word that names one kind or one subset of a part (cauline, floating, lateral, lowest, sterile radiant, allomorphic, axillary, ebracteate stalks, or a narrow synonym such as caudex, phyllode, bracteole) is dropped or folded into a broader class, so an absence becomes 'part absent' for the whole taxon.
remedy: Annotator rule: an absence is grounded only to the most specific class the words name. 'cauline/stem leaves absent' or 'stem/scape leafless' -> cauline leaf PO:0000013. 'phyllodia absent' -> phyllode leaf PO:0025335. 'not bracteolate' -> bracteole PO:0009043. 'ebracteate peduncle' -> bract part_of peduncle. If the qualifier picks out a kind with no term (floating, lateral, allomorphic, sterile radiant, budlike, axillary, very lowest), emit nothing. Never fall back to the general part, and never collapse a narrow synonym into its broader class when the statement is an absence. Extend absence_scope_problem() so that any modifier before the head noun gives 'absence_in_some_members'.
detectable: yes: in an absence row, the source span has a word before the head noun (adjective, position word or selector) that is not part of the grounded bearer's label or synonyms, or the head matched a synonym that is narrower than the class it grounds to
example: 'Cauline leaves absent' in an acaulescent crucifer became leaf absent; it should be cauline leaf PO:0000013 absent

cause: Wordings that existing terms and patterns already cover fail only because a cue, synonym or rule row is missing from the reviewed tables (early caducous, enlarging in fruit, se détachant facilement, at immaturity, nombreux, filling, raceme of racemes, '-less', 'N length of X', 'not or weakly', cell = locule, twig, central spikelet).
remedy: Add rows. Quality rules: 'caducous'/'early caducous' -> deciduous PATO_0001730 (with 'early' not read as a stage); 'enlarging in fruit' -> accrescent FLOPO:0991082; 'se détachant facilement'/'readily detached' -> PATO_0001730. Context words: 'at immaturity' -> immature PATO:0001501; 'central' gets spikelet as an allowed bearer. Count cues: 'nombreux/nombreuses' -> many. Pattern 09 cue: 'filling' -> surrounded by PATO:0005016. Synonyms: 'raceme of racemes' -> PO:0030116; 'twig' -> branch PO:0025073; 'cell' -> locule PO:0025263 inside a fruit or ovary. Ratio cue 'N length of X' (GrassBase) -> length ratio to X, never a count. Negation: read 'not or weakly Q' like 'Q or nearly so' and read '-less' as negated presence. Container rule: 'from one caudex' is not a container.
detectable: yes: rows held as 'no rule' or 'stage' whose span matches one of the new cue strings
example: 'not enlarging in fruit' was held; it should be sepal PO:0009031 accrescent FLOPO:0991082, negated

cause: The absence of a sub-part or a part found on an organ (glands, domatia, stipules, stereids, colleters, annulus, pseudostalk, lobes, blade of a petal, veins of a septum, bristle) is put on the organ that bears it, or the part word is not in the lexicon and falls back to the organ.
remedy: Annotator rule: in 'without X', 'X absent', 'eX-ate' and '<region> without X', X is the bearer of the absence and the organ is only its location (part_of). If X does not ground (flap, pseudostalk, oral setae), emit nothing and never use the clause's organ. Rows to add: domatium FLOPO:0986021; colleter FLOPO:0986023; gland PO:0005656; stereid PO:0030045 (context costa); 'blade' inside a petal, sepal or bract clause -> the lamina of that organ.
detectable: yes: an absence row whose span names a head noun other than the grounded bearer's label or synonyms (absence_scope_problem already returns 'absence_in_some_members' for some of these; extend it to every unmatched head noun)
example: 'domatia absent' became leaf lamina absent; it should be domatium FLOPO:0986021 absent, located on the lamina

cause: A part word whose meaning depends on the family or the flower context is grounded through a general lexicon synonym to the wrong PO class (stone -> seed, spur -> short shoot, ligule, utricle, tepal -> petal, rhizome -> root, stipel -> stipule, axis -> stem, racemes, calyx lobes -> leaf lobe, perichaetial leaves, leafy stem).
remedy: Add context-scoped bearer rows (word, family or section context, PO class). 'stone/pyrene' in a drupe -> endocarp. 'spur' in a flower or lip clause -> floral spur, with short shoot PO:0004701 kept only for woody shoots. 'ligule' in Asteraceae -> ray floret corolla. 'utricle' in Carex -> perigynium PO:0009044. 'tepals' -> tepal, never petal. 'rhizome' -> PO:0004542. 'stipelle' -> stipel PO:0020051, matched before stipule. 'axis/rachis' in an inflorescence paragraph -> inflorescence axis PO:0020122. 'racemes' along a central axis in grasses -> inflorescence branch. 'lobes' after Calyx -> calyx lobe. 'perichaetial leaves' -> PO_0030030. 'leafy stem' in mosses -> gametophore. Remove the generic synonym where it misleads (pyrene -> seed).
detectable: partly: the grounded class differs from the exact source word (synonym match) and the clause, family or heading is on a list of known conflicts
example: 'Spur 1.5-2 mm' after 'Lip ovate' (Angraecum) became short shoot PO_0004701; it should be the floral nectar spur

cause: '<part> not seen / not known / unknown / inconnu / non vu' (missing material) is read as '<part> absent'.
remedy: Prompt: 'If the text says a part was not seen, not known, unknown, not observed, inconnu(e)s or non vu(e)s, write no row for it. It is missing data, not absence.' Annotator: widen _NOT_OBSERVED to all of these forms, including French, and drop any absence or negated row that matches. Also map 'infructescence' to PO:0006342, never to inflorescence.
detectable: yes: regex on the source span (not seen|not known|unknown|not observed|inconnu|non vu)
example: 'Flowers not known' (described from fruiting material) became flower absent; it should give no annotation

cause: A count written inside a word ('N-xed') is not split: a range or 'N- or M-' prefix, an adverb before it, a place word, or a missing suffix row sends it to the measurement path as a number without a unit.
remedy: Run the N-xed split before the measurement parser. Accept 'N-M-xed', 'N- or M-xed' and 'N–M-xed' as count ranges. Skip a leading adverb (unequally) or place word (apex). Rows to add to flora_counted_parts.tsv: 'forked' -> lobe/segment and 'branched' -> branch. Rule: 'N-seriate' -> biseriate FLOPO:0991089 for N=2 and multiseriate FLOPO:0991084 for N>=3, with N kept in RDF. Ground 'segments' of a pinnatipartite leaf to leaf lobe.
detectable: yes: regex \b\d+(\s*[-–]\s*\d+)?(\s*-?\s*or\s*\d+)?-(\w+)\b with the suffix in flora_counted_parts.tsv, on rows held as 'missing unit'
example: 'calyx 5-parted' was held as a length without a unit; it should be a count of 5 lobes with calyx as the container

cause: A heading or contrast word that limits the statement to some members or one state (male/female flowers, sterile/fertile fronds, juvenile/adult, outer/inner, lateral sepals, acroscopic/basiscopic margins, leaflet blades after petiolules) is not carried onto the row.
remedy: Prompt: 'Carry the heading of the paragraph (Male flowers:, Female flowers:, Central spikelet:) and any contrast word (sterile/fertile, juvenile/adult, outer/inner, lateral/median, acroscopic/basiscopic) onto every row it governs, as a qualifier. After petiolules, "blades" are leaflet blades.' Annotator: map these qualifiers through flora_context_words.tsv to bearer_state or position. Hold a row when the paragraph has contrasting headings and the row carries none.
detectable: partly: the description contains 'Male flowers'/'Female flowers', 'sterile ... fertile', 'juvenile ... adult' or 'outer ... inner' headings, and a row taken from that sentence has no state qualifier
example: 'Male flowers ...; sepals 3' became sepal amount 3 for all flowers; it should be sepal count 3 in male flowers

cause: A count that holds per unit (per peduncle, per petiole, per node, per series, per side, per cm) loses that unit or gets the wrong container, or a density is taken for a count.
remedy: Add count_position cues: 'per node'/'par nœud' (per_node), 'in each series' (per_series) and 'at either side' (each_side). Treat 'N per cm'/'par cm' as a density along an axis, never as a count per inflorescence. Annotator: in '<part> ... with N X' or 'N X on <part>', make <part> the container (peduncle, petiole), not the organ the X belong to. Fold a following 'occasionally absent' into the range as 0.
detectable: yes: the span contains 'per', 'par', 'each', 'either side' or 'on <part>', and the container is missing or is the counted organ's own class
example: 'Acorns 1-3' (per peduncle) got fruit as the container; the container should be the peduncle or infructescence

cause: In Carex and grass text, 'bladeless' (bladeless sheaths, uppermost bract nearly bladeless) is read as 'leaf lamina absent' for the taxon.
remedy: Rule: 'bladeless sheath(s)', 'sheaths bladeless' and 'basal sheaths bladeless' -> scale leaf PO:0006003 present, or aphyllopodic FLOPO:0991233 on the culm. '<bract> (nearly) bladeless' stays on the bract as reduced. Never emit leaf or leaf lamina absent from 'bladeless'.
detectable: yes: an absence row on leaf or leaf lamina whose span contains 'bladeless'
example: 'bladeless sheaths at base' became leaf lamina absent; it should be scale leaf present (or aphyllopodic)

cause: The structure of a clause is broken: a transition ('X becoming Y'), a range with alternatives ('A to B or C'), an alternative with its own frequency, or the scope of a disjunction is cut or taken from another clause.
remedy: Keep 'X becoming Y' and '... becoming Z as <part> matures' whole, as a time transition. Never emit a bare 'becoming Y'. Read 'A to B or C' as A-B or A-C. Read a comma-separated 'rarely X and Y' as one operand with frequency 'rarely'. Test for a disjunction only inside the statement's own clause. Drop a union when both operands ground to the same class.
detectable: yes: a span that starts with 'becoming'; a 'to ... or' value list with fewer operands than value words; union operands with the same class
example: 'subcircular to oblong or oblanceolate' lost subcircular; it should be subcircular-to-oblong or subcircular-to-oblanceolate

cause: Numbers or values are misread: 'to L × W' loses the length, 'connate for X mm' becomes the organ's length, an attribute (width, shape) and its value are swapped, or a count or condition is transcribed as a process or as the wrong value.
remedy: Prompt: 'In "to L × W unit", "to" bounds both numbers: L is length, W is width. In "connate/fused for X mm", X is how far the fusion runs, not the organ's length. For "N mm broad/long/thick", the quality is the attribute (width, length, thickness) with N. For "Fruit obovoid", the quality is the value, never the word "shape". Turn "only N flowers developing into fruits" into a count of fruits. Turn "when crushed" into a condition.' Table: add a 'crushed' condition row to flora_context_words.tsv.
detectable: partly: '×' with only one number kept; 'connate|fused for \d' bound to length; quality 'shape' or 'broad' with a number
example: 'to 28 × 10 cm' became length max 10 cm; it should be length up to 28 cm and width up to 10 cm

cause: A negated quality or relation of a part that is present ('never palmate', 'dots absent', 'not attached to', 'ribs absent') is turned into the absence of the part.
remedy: 'never Q' and 'not Q' -> Q negated on the subject. 'dots absent', 'without dots' and 'epunctate' -> punctate PATO:0001512 negated on the named surface. 'ribs absent'/'without ribs' -> ribbed negated. 'not attached to X' -> a negated relation. When the absent word is not a PO part, never fall back to absence of the bearer.
detectable: yes: an absence row whose span head (dots, ribs, palmate, attached) is a quality or relation word, not the bearer
example: 'dots absent' became leaf lamina absent; it should be lamina surface punctate PATO:0001512, negated

cause: Hedged or reduced wording ('nearly leafless', 'without significant palea', 'non visible', 'not distinctly') is read as absence.
remedy: 'nearly/almost leafless' and 'subaphyllous' -> reduced (decreased size or few, or scale leaf PO:0006003), never absent. 'without significant/conspicuous X' and 'non visible/not visible/obscure' -> inconspicuous PATO_0000464. 'not distinctly Q' -> Q negated with qualifier approximately. Add these as hedge cues that block absence.
detectable: yes: an absence row whose span contains nearly, almost, sub-, significant, conspicuous, distinctly or visible
example: 'Calice non visible' (Mimosa pudica) became calyx absent; it should be calyx inconspicuous

cause: Bamboo and grass sheath parts ('auricles and oral setae absent', 'culm sheath') are grounded to stipule.
remedy: Rows: 'auricle(s)' in grass or bamboo text -> leaf sheath auricle PO:0020106; 'culm sheath' -> leaf sheath PO:0020104; 'oral setae' -> no term (hold), never awn. Remove any auricle -> stipule route for Poaceae.
detectable: yes: bearer stipule PO:0020041 on a row whose span contains auricle, oral setae or sheath
example: 'auricles and oral setae absent' became stipule absent; it should be leaf sheath auricle PO:0020106 absent, with oral setae held back

cause: Frequency, degree or gradient words (rarement, mostly, upward) are taken as the quality or the wrong qualifier.
remedy: Prompt: 'rarely, often, usually and rarement are frequency qualifiers of another statement, never the quality. "upward" alone is a gradient along the axis (context word upper part). "mostly adnate" says how much of the part is fused (degree), not how often.' Annotator: drop rows whose quality is a frequency or direction word with no value.
detectable: yes: the quality span is only a frequency adverb or 'upward' (PATO_0000044, PATO_0000370), or 'mostly' maps to frequency 'usually' before a fusion word
example: 'rarement' became leaflet frequency PATO_0000044; it should be fb:frequency on the statement it modifies

cause: A process quality (up, duration, continuous) is grounded on a plant structure, which makes the class unsatisfiable.
remedy: Annotator check: reject any quality under PATO 'process quality' on a PO or FLOPO structure bearer. Table remaps: up PATO_0000370 -> ascending PATO_0104355 (or curved if the text says upcurved); 'saisonnières' (stems) -> annual life span PATO_0104360; 'continuous' -> decurrent FLOPO_0991162/PATO_0001984 when continuous with the rachis, otherwise reject.
detectable: yes: the quality is a subclass of process quality in quality.obo and the bearer is a structure
example: 'points upwards' (keel) became up PATO_0000370; it should be ascending PATO_0104355

cause: 'glaucous' is grounded to green instead of glaucous.
remedy: Lexicon row 'glaucous' -> glaucous PATO_0104277. Remove any glaucous -> green (FLOPO_0988006) synonym.
detectable: yes: span contains 'glaucous' and the quality is green
example: 'slightly glaucous' fruit became green; it should be glaucous PATO_0104277

cause: In '<colour> pubescent/puberulous/tomentose', the colour of the hairs is given to the organ.
remedy: Rule: a colour word placed right before a hair word describes the hairs. Emit organ + pubescence, plus trichome part_of organ + colour. Never emit organ + colour.
detectable: yes: a colour row whose span has a colour word followed by a hair word (pubescent, puberulous, hairy, tomentose, villous)
example: 'densely yellow pubescent' petiole became petiole yellow; it should be petiole pubescent, with trichome yellow

cause: Other: a reference back to an earlier noun is bound to the wrong part (a length given to absent awns; an elided 'the terminal' leaflet).
remedy: Prompt: 'A size or quality with no noun ("longer ones N mm", "the terminal ...") refers back to the last plural noun named in the clause (teeth, lobes, leaflets). Never bind it to a part just stated absent.' Annotator: hold a measurement on a part that has an absence row in the same description.
detectable: partly: a measurement row and an absence row on the same bearer in one description
example: 'awns absent ... longer ones N mm' gave a length to the awns; the length belongs to the involucre teeth
